alignments.note: Fronted nominal (casus pendens) to *appearance*. The supplied *as for* is no longer part of this unit: no morpheme stands on the fronted phrase to license it, so it is its own `added` unit (rules 16, 30).

The supplied *as for* answers to no morpheme. מַרְאֵיהֶם is a bare noun with a suffix, carrying no object marker and no preposition, so rule 16's limit applies as it does to an appositional *even* before a phrase no marker marks, and rule 30 leaves the expression `added`. It is not folded into the fronted noun to avoid that, for the reason rule 42 gives about a surplus *and*: the words are written beside that rendering rather than inside it. Headed on *as*, the token carrying the lexeme (rule 24). Contrast 10:13, where a real fronting לְ carries *As for*.
Verbless possessive clause: the possessive preposition is what makes it possessive and carries the *had* (rule 43).
Comparative particle to *as*; the ASV spends a second word on אֲשֶׁר, so rule 2 splits the pair rather than fusing it (rule 30).
The relative takes the *if* of the ASV's *as if*.
Verb with its auxiliary, headed on the lexical predicate (rule 24).
The ASV writes *a wheel*, so the article has no *the* to take (rule 29).
The indefinite *a* belongs to the noun that licenses it (rule 15).
בְּתוֹךְ rendered by the single English word *within*: the two morphemes share one unit headed on the lexeme-bearing תָּוֶךְ (rule 30). The ASV's margin gives the Hebrew as *in the midst of*.
The ASV writes *a wheel* with no *the* (rule 29).
The indefinite *a* belongs to the noun (rule 15).

review_notes: Reconciliation patch. The supplied *as for* is now its own `added` unit instead of joining מַרְאֵיהֶם. Rule 16 marks a supplied word of that family `added` where the phrase it introduces carries no marker, and this chapter already applied that reasoning in 10:12 to the bare noun אוֹפַנֵּיהֶם; מַרְאֵיהֶם is the same shape, a noun and a suffix with no marker and no preposition on it.

Rule 33 was the earlier basis and does not reach: it gives a supplied function word to a noun whose own case-function licenses it, and a topicalized nominal's fronting is not such a case-function. Rule 16's Jebusites example gives *as for* to the marker because nothing else answers to the two words, which tells against the fronted noun being a candidate.

The fronted noun keeps only *appearance* and its suffix keeps *their* (rule 18). Every other unit stands as the verse pass returned it. Partition re-verified: 17 source ids across 17 units, all 19 target ids used exactly once.
Contrast 10:13, where the fronting לְ of לָאוֹפַנִּים is a present morpheme and carries *As for*.
